note: Private campground on a hillside off D Ave a mile south of Wadena, with a small catch-and-release fishing pond, playground, walking trail to a Pheasants Forever prairie, and storm shelters in the laundry room and owner's garage. Mostly seasonal sites: the operator counts 60 seasonal sites on a 61-site map, and nightly guests get seasonal sites not yet occupied. --Claude
summary: Confirmed $35 a night (2027, tax in), full hookups 50/35/20 amp; added showers, dump, laundry, wifi, phone booking; site count 50 -> 61 (operator map). Price gate passes, but it reads as mostly seasonal: drop candidate on long-stay test 4 for AWH to decide. Google 4.1 from 21.
flags: DROP CANDIDATE (mostly seasonal, long-stay test 4): the operator's home page counts '60 seasonal sites'. Its map numbers 61 sites. The rules give nightly guests only what is left: 'Until a seasonal unit is placed on the site, campground owners have the discretion to rent the site.' A Google review (Ryan Cummings, 2/5, '7 years ago') reads 'Tiny sites. Couldnt even really set up yard games. Nowhere to park. Seemed like the majority of campers are seasonals with nice decks and their own lp tanks.' On NAIP nearly every site holds a parked trailer. What the operator leads with: '2027 Ways To Stay' lists nightly first, but the page also carries the 2027 Seasonal Agreement and seasonal deposit dates. I read it as mostly seasonal: under 1 site in 10 is sold nightly. It is not iffy on reviews (Google 4.1/21, other reviews 5/5), so it is not the automatic under-4-stars drop. The entry was kept on AWH's 2026-10-02 read but has no --AWH note.

REVIEWS: Google Maps 4.1 from 21 reviews (under 25). RV Life lists it unrated (price tier 1). Reviews read: Tim Flagg 5/5 ('5 years ago': 'Awesome Campground! I spent a week here ... Sites are large and lots of privacy'); Hance Throckmorton 5/5 ('2 years ago': 'Good place to camp! They have bathrooms and showers'); Mark Powers 5/5 ('5 years ago': 'Clean, organized, friendly campers, limited space so call ahead!'); Ryan Cummings 2/5 (above).
PRICE GATE: passes. $35 a night tax included (2027 rates on the operator's page). No gateway within 40 km; the family has never stayed.

LONG-STAY TESTS: 1 seasonal-only sites: effectively yes, all 60 are seasonal sites with nightly use of unfilled ones. 2 posted nightly rate: yes, $35. 3 monthly-only: no. 4 nightly share: likely under 1 in 10 (see drop candidate). 5 homes or lots for sale: none seen.
PRESENCE: OK on the website rule, a working WordPress site with phone 563-774-2067 (matches stored and Google). Google has fewer than 25 reviews. No online booking.

WATERFRONT (confirms not waterfront): the catch-and-release pond is about 50 x 55 m on NAIP (~0.2 ha, well under 5 acres), so it is a pond with no view value. Sites 36-40 are across the campground road from it and P1-P7 across the 'Limited Access' drive. A creek runs along the east property line outside the sites, under trees.
